backlog_low_priority.purpose: 2026-09-04 True Home + Mobile Map Simplification: independent Codex screenshot review (factory/state/expansion/true-home-map-codex-review-final.json) repeatedly scored HOME_GAME_FEEL below threshold across 3 rounds (68/68/67, need >=80) with the same root-cause finding each time: True Home reads as 'an elegant learning-site card menu' rather than a game hub, because it has 'no character, no sense of an ongoing world, no world-state connection.' CSS-only fixes (breathing animation, sparkle, explicit play-button affordance, Japanese microcopy) measurably helped other axes but could not move this one — Codex's own comparison note is that the missing ingredient is a character/mascot presence, which is explicitly GPT's domain, not something to keep chasing with layout tricks.
backlog_low_priority.current_problem: True Home is 3 flat rounded-rectangle cards (a photo card + 2 icon cards) with no character or figure of any kind, unlike Home-screen conventions in Animal Crossing / Duolingo / Pokemon spinoffs where a character or avatar anchors the title/hub screen and visually signals 'a world you return to,' not a menu.
backlog_low_priority.required_subject: A single small, friendly mascot/guide character (or a loose set of 2-3 alternate poses) that could sit on or beside the primary '社会を冒険する' (go adventure in society) card — e.g., peeking from a corner, waving, or looking toward the town image. No specific character has been designed for this game yet; propose something warm and simple that fits a clay-diorama town of many different professions (not tied to any one profession/world) so it can be reused as a persistent Home/brand figure across future sessions.
backlog_low_priority.required_style: Match existing JIBUN CHOICE series style — miniature clay-diorama look, warm rounded forms, soft lighting, no photorealism (see reference_assets). Should read clearly at small size (mobile card corner, roughly 80-140px).
backlog_low_priority.composition: Small enough to sit within or beside the primary card without covering the title text or the existing play-button chip (bottom-right of that card is already occupied — see src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx home-card-play). A bottom-left or top-left placement, or a version designed to sit just outside/below the card, would avoid collision.
backlog_low_priority.aspect_ratio: flexible, roughly square or portrait, whatever suits a single small figure
backlog_low_priority.safe_area: n/a — full figure should be visible, no internal cropping needed given the small footprint

backlog_low_priority.purpose: 2026-09-04 Map Architecture Human Decision selected 'A: ONE CONTINUOUS WORLD' as the base architecture specifically to fix the current production Map's Human Visual Review finding (district illustrations at mismatched scale/camera-angle/lighting reading as 'assets collaged together'). Two low-cost prototypes tested this: A2 (public/dev-prototypes/prototype-a2-semantic-zoom.html) and A3 (prototype-a3-cohesive-world.html), the latter applying CSS-only integration technique (feathered masks, unified light-gradient overlay, shared filter) to the EXISTING separately-generated district illustrations. An independent Codex review of A3 (factory/state/expansion/map-a3-codex-review-2026-09-04.json) confirmed the Human's own advance warning: VISUAL_COHESION scored 24/100 (threshold 90) — 'reused district illustrations share a similarly soft palette but not the same camera angle, scale, or lighting... background feathering only softens the cut line, it doesn't resolve the projection and scale mismatch.' Codex's own conclusion: 'a genuinely new continuous world-base illustration built at one consistent camera angle/scale/light source is needed — placement and blending of existing assets alone cannot resolve the projection/scale mismatch.' Following that finding, the Human supplied a detailed brief (2026-09-05) covering mobile framing, future-expansion, district integration, perspective/scale, composition, embedded-UI exclusion, art style, and output planning — captured in the fields below.
backlog_low_priority.current_problem: The 4 existing district illustrations + town-hero were each independently generated (at different sessions, different implied camera distance/angle — e.g. the center town is a wide aerial view of an entire town, while district illustrations are close-up dioramas of a few buildings). No CSS technique (masking, feathering, shared color-grade filter, drop-shadow grounding) can fix a baked-in projection/scale mismatch between raster images.
backlog_low_priority.required_subject: ONE continuous illustration depicting the JIBUN CHOICE world's known geography in a single frame: town center, harbor (港), forest/river (森と川), station area (駅前), and hill/civic area (丘の上). Existing illustrations (public/assets/districts/*.png, public/assets/town-hero.png) are supplied as STYLE/MOTIF reference only (the clay-diorama look, color palette, general idea of what each district contains) — do not copy their composition or projection. This is a new single composition, not a collage of the old ones.
backlog_low_priority.district_integration: Include all 5: town center, harbor, forest/river, station area, hill/civic area. PROHIBITED: presenting these as 5 independent islands/cards/dioramas arranged within one image (this is exactly the current production problem, restated at illustration-authoring time so it cannot recur in the new asset). No hard boundary lines between districts. Districts connect and differentiate through natural, continuous variation in terrain, road, river, rail, building density, and vegetation — the transition FROM one district INTO the next should itself read as part of the world, not a seam.
backlog_low_priority.perspective_scale: Single camera angle and single perspective across the entire illustration. Consistent building scale and consistent character/object scale throughout (no wide aerial-view area next to a close-up diorama area). Single light direction and consistent shadow softness across the whole piece (per factory/rules/visual-design-system.md §SHADOW/§DEPTH). This is the single most important requirement — it is the specific property CSS-only integration (tried in Prototype A3) could not achieve after the fact.
backlog_low_priority.composition: A large pannable canvas — the viewport will only ever show a portion at a time (confirmed workable via the A3 prototype's camera model). Important landmarks should not all cluster in one spot; distribute points of visual interest so that panning toward any of them is rewarded with something worth looking at — but the layout itself must never become a navigation puzzle or require understanding correct paths/geography. The goal is purely 'something here makes me want to touch it' and 'there's probably more off-screen,' not spatial complexity or route-finding.
backlog_low_priority.mobile_initial_viewport: On a 375px-wide mobile viewport at first load, the town center should be the primary focus, with roughly 2 adjacent districts partially visible at the screen edges (not fully shown) — enough to make it intuitively obvious the world continues beyond the frame. Must avoid both failure modes: (a) showing all 5 districts at once in the initial view (too dense, defeats panning-as-discovery), and (b) showing only the town center with nothing else even partially visible (reads as a single static image, not 'one continuous world you can move through').
backlog_low_priority.future_expansion: Do not leave 'reserved space for future districts' as plain empty terrain — that reads as an unfinished gap, not an inviting unknown. Instead, have road, river, rail, terrain, coastline, and vegetation continue naturally toward the canvas edges, so those edges themselves suggest 'the world keeps going past here' (consistent with the existing fog/silhouette 'discovery' visual language already used elsewhere in the app, which can be composited on top of these naturally-continuing edges later). Avoid pinning major landmarks too close to the canvas edge, so a future expansion pass has room to extend the world without needing to move or rework existing landmarks.
backlog_low_priority.no_embedded_ui: Do NOT draw any of the following into the illustration — these are composited by the application on top of the base art at runtime, not baked into it: 'NEW' badges, question marks, fire icons, buttons, text labels, UI badges, or any gameplay/event markers. The illustration is pure environment/world art with no interface elements.
backlog_low_priority.required_style: Match existing JIBUN CHOICE series style: handmade clay / miniature diorama look, warm rounded forms, a slightly handcrafted (not machine-perfect) texture, bright and inviting, child-friendly but not babyish. Explicitly NOT photorealistic, and NOT a generic polished Pixar/Disney-style character-rendering look. Any human figures are minimal and exist only as part of the background world (scale/life cues), never a focal character — this illustration must not introduce or imply a new brand character or mascot (that remains a separate HUMAN_PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED matter per factory/rules/product-identity-gate.md, unrelated to and not to be conflated with this environment-art request).
backlog_low_priority.aspect_ratio: First draft: wide landscape, approximately 2:1. Final aspect ratio is NOT locked yet — to be decided only after checking the first draft against both the 375px mobile pan viewport (per mobile_initial_viewport above) and desktop usage.
backlog_low_priority.reference_assets_usage_note: Style/motif reference only (palette, clay-diorama craft quality, what kind of buildings/objects belong to each district) — do NOT reference their composition, camera angle, or projection; those are exactly what this new illustration must NOT inherit from them.
backlog_low_priority.safe_area: n/a — full-bleed world background, not a masked vignette
backlog_low_priority.output_planning: Expect an iterative process: first draft at ~2:1 landscape, reviewed against the mobile_initial_viewport framing and a few desktop widths, aspect ratio and possibly composition adjusted before treating any version as final.

revision_note_2026_09_04: Claude's initial self-audit classified forest_trees as D (keep-candidate, low priority) and all 4 district clusters as POST_RELEASE_ART_BACKLOG (not blocking). An INDEPENDENT Codex vision audit (factory/state/art/art-ownership-codex-audit.json), shown only screenshots with no access to Claude's classification, disagreed on both counts: it classified forest_trees as E (not D) and judged all 4 district illustration clusters (harbor/forest/station/hill) as any_public_blocker=true, reasoning that the Home screen is the app's primary, first-impression surface — not a deep/secondary screen — so a visible style mismatch there counts as a real public blocker, not backlog. Because Claude has an inherent conflict of interest auditing its own work, this file defers to the independent Codex verdict: forest-district-illustration has been moved from backlog into the primary (blocking) requests list below, and all 4 requests are now marked public_blocker=true. No image was generated or redrawn by Claude to resolve this — per directive §16, that is explicitly GPT's job; these requests remain open until fulfilled.
